document.title: Ripple effect modelling of supplier disruption: integrated Markov chain and dynamic Bayesian network approach
document.abstract: The ripple effect could occur when a disruption in supplier base can not be localised and a disruption in supplier base consequences propagate downstream the supply chain ( SC ) adversely affecting the performance . While stress-testing of SC designs and assessment of SC designs vulnerability to disruptions in single-echelon-single-event setting is desirable and indeed critical for some firms , modeling the ripple effect impact in multi-echelon-correlated-events systems is becoming increasingly important . Notably , ripple effect assessment in multi-stage SCs is particularly challenged by consideration of both vulnerability and recoverability capabilities at individual firms in the network . We construct a new model based on integrating Discrete-Time Markov Chain ( DTMC ) and Dynamic Bayesian Network ( DBN ) model to quantify The ripple effect . We use DTMC to model the recovery and vulnerability of suppliers . a new model based on integrating Discrete-Time Markov Chain ( DTMC ) and Dynamic Bayesian Network ( DBN ) model is then equalized with a DBN model in order to simulate the propagation behavior of supplier disruption in the supply chain ( SC ) . Finally , We propose a metric that quantifies the ripple effect of supplier disruption on manufacturer in terms of total expected utility and service level . a metric that quantifies the ripple effect of supplier disruption on manufacturer in terms of total expected utility and service level is examined and tested using two case-studies . The findings suggest that a new model based on integrating Discrete-Time Markov Chain ( DTMC ) and Dynamic Bayesian Network ( DBN ) model can be of value in revealing latent high-risk paths in the supply chain ( SC ) , analysing the performance impact of both a disruption and a disruption propagation , and prioritizing the contingency and recovery policies .
